subtitle: From Hasan Gangu to Alauddin Bahman Shah, a Deccan Crown is Forged

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of Alauddin Bahman Shah standing before Gulbarga fort, stormy Deccan sky behind
panels.action: Alauddin Bahman Shah stands in regal armor before the massive stone walls of Gulbarga, one hand resting on a sheathed sword, the other open to the darkening Deccan horizon, as wind whips his cloak around him.

dialogue.text: In the troubled Deccan of 1347, a field commander named Hasan Gangu cast off Delhi’s shadow and rose as Alauddin Bahman Shah, founding a kingdom whose truth lies deeper than its legends.

i18n.hi: सन् 1347 के अशांत दक्कन में, हसन गंगू नाम का एक फौजी अफ़सर दिल्ली की परछाईं से निकलकर अलाउद्दीन बहमनशाह बना, और एक ऐसा सल्तनत खड़ी की जिसकी सच्चाई उसकी क़िस्सों से गहरी है।

panels.shot: bird's-eye view of the Deccan plateau with routes from Delhi snaking south
panels.action: The Deccan plateau stretches under a hazy sky, crisscrossed by dusty roads; tiny caravans, marching columns, and scattered forts hint at a vast empire straining to hold its southern lands.

dialogue.text: By the 1340s, the Delhi Sultanate’s reach had pushed deep into the Deccan, but its grip was weakening. Costly campaigns, harsh experiments, and distance frayed the bonds between Delhi and its southern soldiers.

i18n.hi: 1340 के दशक तक दिल्ली सल्तनत की पहुँच दक्कन तक धँस चुकी थी, लेकिन पकड़ ढीली पड़ रही थी। महँगे अभियान, सख़्त प्रयोग और दूरियाँ, दिल्ली और उसके दक्खनी सिपाहियों के रिश्ते घिस रहे थे।

panels.shot: wide shot of Daulatabad fort looming over rocky hills at dusk
panels.action: The steep, walled heights of Daulatabad fort rise from the bare rock, its gates closed, tiny figures of soldiers silhouetted on the battlements as the sun sinks in a dusty orange haze.

dialogue.text: At Daulatabad, the Tughluq experiment of ruling the Deccan from a second capital had left wounds. Barani notes officers unpaid, garrisons restless, and commanders who measured loyalty against survival.

i18n.hi: दौलताबाद में, दक्कन को दूसरी राजधानी से चलाने का तुग़लक़ी प्रयोग गहरे घाव छोड़ गया। बरनी लिखता है कि अफ़सरों को तनख़ाह नहीं, छावनियाँ बेचैन, और सरदार वफ़ादारी को ज़िंदा रहने के तराज़ू में तौलते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of young Hasan Gangu among rank-and-file soldiers in a dusty camp
panels.action: A younger Hasan Gangu stands in worn mail among a circle of tired soldiers in a Deccan camp, his hands rough from drill, listening intently as older officers argue over orders from distant Delhi.

dialogue.text: Barani calls him a man of humble origin, a field worker raised into the army. In the Deccan camps, Hasan Gangu learned dust, discipline, and the hard lessons of serving a far-off court.

i18n.hi: बरनी उसे नीची ज़ात का आदमी कहता है, खेत मज़दूर जो फ़ौज में उठा लिया गया। दक्कन की छावनियों में हसन गंगू ने धूल, अनुशासन और दूर बैठे दरबार की ख़िदमत के सख़्त सबक सीखे।

panels.shot: close-up on Hasan’s face lit by campfire, half in shadow
panels.action: Firelight flickers across Hasan’s face as he sits by a campfire, one side lit warm, the other lost in shadow, eyes steady as he watches a parchment order burn in the flames.

dialogue.speaker: alauddin_bahman_shah
dialogue.text: If they command without justice, how long must we obey?

i18n.hi: अगर हुज़ूर बेइंसाफ़ी से हुक्म दें, तो हम कब तक मानते रहें?

panels.shot: dynamic wide of a rebel assembly of Deccani amirs in a rugged landscape
panels.action: On a stony plateau under a harsh sun, armored Deccani amirs stand in a tense circle, banners drooping in the still air as they argue, their horses tethered nearby and distant hills framing the scene.

dialogue.text: In this unsettled world, Deccani amirs began to defy Delhi. Eaton notes how the south’s military elites, mostly long-serving officers, turned rebellion into a bid for their own sovereignty.

i18n.hi: इसी उथल-पुथल में दक्खनी अमीरों ने दिल्ली का कहना काटना शुरू किया। ईटन बताता है कि दक्षिण के फ़ौजी सरदार, ज़्यादातर पुराने अफ़सर, बग़ावत को अपनी खुद की बादशाहत की दावेदारी बना बैठे।

panels.shot: mid-wide of Hasan Gangu speaking to a small cluster of officers in a fortified courtyard
panels.action: Within a rough stone courtyard, Hasan Gangu faces a knot of armored officers, his stance firm but modest, as they lean in to hear him above the distant echo of drills and clanging metal.

dialogue.text: Hasan rose among them as a capable commander, trusted in battle and negotiation. Barani records his service under the Tughluqs, yet it is in this moment that he begins to become more than a servant.

i18n.hi: हसन इन्हीं में एक काबिल सिपहसालार बनकर उभरा, जंग में और सुलह में भरोसेमंद। बरनी उसके तुग़लकों के अधीन ख़िदमत का ज़िक्र करता है, लेकिन यही वो घड़ी है जब वो महज़ मुलाज़िम से आगे बढ़ने लगता है।

panels.shot: interior wide of a simple hall where a local leader Ismail Mukh is being acclaimed on a makeshift throne
panels.action: In a plain stone hall, a modest, hastily raised chair stands like a throne as Deccani chiefs bow to a dignified Ismail Mukh, who sits with reluctance, hands resting lightly on his knees.

dialogue.text: When the Tughluq hold cracked, the Deccani nobles first set up Ismail Mukh as their leader. Ferishta names him, a figurehead for revolt, while Delhi’s writ shrank to roads and garrisons.

i18n.hi: जब तुग़लक़ों की पकड़ टूटी, तो दक्खनी सरदारों ने पहले इस्माइल मुख को अपना सरदार बनाया। फ़िरीश्ता उसका नाम देता है, बग़ावत का झंडाबरदार, जबकि दिल्ली का हुक्म बस सड़कों और किलों तक सिमट गया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Hasan Gangu standing respectfully before Ismail Mukh in the same hall
panels.action: Hasan Gangu stands before Ismail Mukh, head slightly bowed, hands clasped, as the older man regards him thoughtfully; behind them, amirs watch, weighing the balance between name and power.

dialogue.text: Yet power on the ground rested with Hasan and the rebel commanders. Ferishta describes councils where they quietly measured Ismail’s symbolic rule against Hasan’s command of men and fortresses.

i18n.hi: पर असली ताक़त ज़मीन पर हसन और बाग़ी सिपहसालारों के हाथ में थी। फ़िरीश्ता उन मजलिसों का वर्णन करता है जहाँ वो चुपचाप इस्माइल की नाम भर बादशाहत को हसन की फौजों और क़िलों पर पकड़ से तौलते थे।

panels.shot: intimate medium of Ismail placing his hand on Hasan’s shoulder in a dim audience chamber
panels.action: In a dim chamber lit by a single lamp, Ismail Mukh rests a gentle hand on Hasan’s shoulder, while Hasan looks surprised, almost resisting, the stone walls closing around their private decision.

dialogue.text: According to Ferishta, the choice was stark: a fragile symbol or a tested general. Ismail is said to have abdicated, asking Hasan to lead, so that the new Deccan state might survive the storms to come.

i18n.hi: फ़िरीश्ता के मुताबिक़ चुनौत साफ़ थी: नाज़ुक निशान या आज़माया हुआ सरदार। कहते हैं इस्माइल ने ख़ुद ताज छोड़कर हसन से क़यादत की दरख़्वास्त की, ताकि नया दक्खनी मुल्क आने वाले तूफ़ानों में टिक सके।

panels.shot: epic wide of the coronation ground near Gulbarga with gathered amirs and soldiers
panels.action: On open ground near Gulbarga, under a broad sky, rows of armored amirs and soldiers form a vast semi-circle as Hasan Gangu, robed in white over mail, stands on a raised platform beside a simple canopy.

dialogue.text: On 3 August 1347, near Gulbarga, the field commander stepped forward to become a king. The day marked not just a ceremony, but the birth of a Deccan sultanate independent of Delhi.

i18n.hi: 3 अगस्त 1347 को, गुलबर्गा के पास, मैदान का यह अफ़सर आगे बढ़ा और बादशाह बन गया। वो दिन सिर्फ़ रस्म नहीं, बल्कि दिल्ली से आज़ाद एक दक्खनी सल्तनत की पैदाइश थी।

panels.shot: low-angle close-medium of Hasan as he receives the ceremonial turban and takes a new name
panels.action: From a low angle, we see Hasan as an elder amir winds a rich turban around his head; his eyes are lifted, jaw set, as attendants hold a sword and a cloak ready at his side.

dialogue.text: Hasan Gangu took the throne-name Alauddin Bahman Shah. The title echoed older Persian lineages, a deliberate claim that this new kingdom would stand among the great houses of Islam.

i18n.hi: हसन गंगू ने तख़्त का नाम रखा अलाउद्दीन बहमनशाह। ये ख़िताब पुराने फ़ारसी ख़ानदानों की गूँज था, साफ़ एलान कि ये नया मुल्क इस्लामी सल्तनतों की बड़ी हवेलियों में जगह चाहता है।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Alauddin Bahman Shah’s hand grasping the hilt of a sheathed sword
panels.action: A close view shows Alauddin Bahman Shah’s hand tightening around the hilt of an unsheathed-but-resting sword, the leather-wrapped grip worn from use, the metal fittings newly polished.

dialogue.speaker: alauddin_bahman_shah
dialogue.text: From today, this land shall not be a province, but a kingdom.

i18n.hi: आज से ये ज़मीन सूबा नहीं, खुद अपना राज्य है।

panels.shot: wide of Gulbarga’s walls and emerging cityscape under construction
panels.action: Gulbarga’s thick new walls rise from the rocky plain; inside, scaffolds climb around mosques and palaces, workers hauling stone as soldiers drill in courtyards, the city taking shape around the citadel.

dialogue.text: Alauddin Bahman Shah chose Gulbarga as his capital. The city’s walls, palaces, and congregational mosque began to grow, staking the Bahmani claim in stone across the Deccan.

i18n.hi: अलाउद्दीन बहमनशाह ने गुलबर्गा को राजधानी चुना। शहर की दीवारें, महल और जामा मस्जिद उठने लगे, पत्थर पर पूरे दक्कन में बहमनी दावा दर्ज होने लगा।

panels.shot: macro close-up of an early Bahmani copper coin on a craftsman’s palm
panels.action: In a coiner’s workroom, a weathered hand holds a freshly struck copper coin, its inscriptions crisp, the small disc catching the light as other coins lie stacked beside simple dies and hammers.

dialogue.text: Copper coins from Gulbarga bear his name and titles, the metal testimony of sovereignty. Where myths spin stories, these coins silently confirm a new state issuing its own authority.

i18n.hi: गुलबर्गा की ताम्बे की सिक्कों पर उसका नाम और अलक़ाब खुदे हैं, धातु में ढली बादशाही की गवाही। जहाँ दास्तानें किस्से बुनती हैं, ये सिक्के चुपचाप नए राज्य की खुद की हुकूमत साबित करते हैं।

panels.shot: interior wide of Alauddin on a simple throne hearing petitions from Deccani soldiers and settlers
panels.action: In a spacious hall, Alauddin Bahman Shah sits on a modest throne, leaning forward as Deccani soldiers, merchants, and clerics stand in ordered lines before him, each bringing petitions and grievances.

dialogue.text: Eaton describes how the Deccan’s society began to reshape around this court. Old soldiers, traders, and scholars sought favor and order from a sultan who had once shared their hardships.

i18n.hi: ईटन लिखता है कि दक्कन का समाज इस नए दरबार के इर्दगिर्द फिर से ढलने लगा। पुराने सिपाही, सौदागर और आलिम, उसी सुल्तान से इनायत और क़ानून तलाशने लगे जो कभी उनकी ही तरह मुसीबतें झेल चुका था।

panels.shot: moody wide of a distant battlefield between Bahmani and southern forces, seen from afar
panels.action: From a distant ridge, we see two dense armies facing each other on a wide plain, banners of different colors snapping in the wind, cavalry lines tense but still, the air heavy with impending clash.

dialogue.text: In later decades, Bahmani rulers would fight Vijayanagara and others in brutal campaigns. Ferishta writes of devastating warfare in the Carnatic, and of captured soldiers sometimes converted and drawn into new armies.

i18n.hi: आने वाले दशकों में बहमनी सुल्तान विजयनगर और दूसरे दुश्मनों से ख़ूँरेज़ जंगें लड़ेंगे। फ़िरीश्ता कारनाटक की उजाड़ कर देने वाली लड़ाइयों का ज़िक्र करता है, और उन फौजियों का भी जो क़ैद से निकलकर इस्लाम कबूल कर नई फौजों में भर लिए गए।

panels.shot: evening medium of an older Alauddin Bahman Shah on the ramparts of Gulbarga, looking out
panels.action: An older Alauddin Bahman Shah stands on Gulbarga’s ramparts at dusk, cloak gathered around him, gazing over the city’s rooftops and walls as lamps begin to flicker to life below.

dialogue.text: Alauddin ruled until 1358, laying the frame of a kingdom others would expand, fracture, and fight over. Barani’s field worker had become the founding sultan of a line that reshaped the Deccan.

i18n.hi: अलाउद्दीन 1358 तक राज करता रहा, उस सल्तनत की बुनियाद डालकर जिसे बाद के लोग बढ़ाएंगे, तोड़ेंगे और फिर उसी पर लड़ेंगे। बरनी का खेत मज़दूर अब वो पहला सुल्तान था जिसने दक्कन का नक्शा बदल दिया।

panels.shot: slow push-in close-up on Alauddin’s contemplative face, half-lit by lamplight
panels.action: In close-up, Alauddin Bahman Shah’s lined face is lit by soft lamplight, eyes thoughtful, lips set in a quiet, unreadable expression as darkness gathers around him.

dialogue.text: Legends later wrapped him in noble ancestry and miracle tales, yet coins, chronicles, and the stone of Gulbarga still recall a harsher truth: a field worker who seized a crown, and a kingdom born from fracture.

i18n.hi: बाद की दास्तानों ने उसे ऊँचे ख़ानदानों और करामातों में लपेट दिया, पर सिक्के, तवारीख़ और गुलबर्गा का पत्थर आज भी कड़वी सच्चाई बताते हैं: खेत का मज़दूर जिसने ताज छीना, और दरारों से जन्मा एक राज्य।

title_i18n.en: The Field Worker Crowned at Gulbarga
title_i18n.hi: गुलबर्गा में खेत मज़दूर का ताज

subtitle_i18n.en: From Hasan Gangu to Alauddin Bahman Shah, a Deccan Crown is Forged
subtitle_i18n.hi: हसन गंगू से अलाउद्दीन बहमनशाह तक, दक्कन का ताज ढलता है
